done_when: Close checks each --dismiss against the item's open findings before it runs tests or review, and accepts a dismissal of an open finding from an earlier round

known.title: Dismissal evidence can be tied to the wrong commit
Retaining an omitted finding can invalidate the required review check
Check dismissal numbers after reconciling the item's remote review

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - The default branch adds an evidence line, and close merges it into a behind pull request while reusing the earlier review.
This validates the evidence against the new head, but a reused review retains its older commit at src/forge/close.py:317. The later dismissal check uses that older commit as its evidence baseline (src/forge/review.py:644). If the cited file or line did not exist then, subsequent edits to the evidence are treated as an addition, so the dismissal can continue to suppress the same serious finding after its proof changes.
findings.title: Dismissal evidence can be tied to the wrong commit

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A worker restores a previously reviewed file to its base version while retaining other changes, then dismisses its old finding when the repair review omits it.
The repair review computes its fingerprint before this line appends the old finding (src/forge/review.py:1050). Because that file is no longer in the branch diff, the required check recomputes a different fingerprint from the saved finding list and rejects the review as out of date (src/forge/prcheck.py:462). The dismissal is recorded, but close cannot complete until the record is refreshed.
findings.title: Retaining an omitted finding can invalidate the required review check

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A teammate reviews the item on another machine while this machine retains an older worktree.
The number is checked against the locally loaded review before remote reconciliation at src/forge/close.py:284. Forge's next view can show the newer remote finding (tests/test_board_counts.py:356), yet close rejects its number if the local review has no findings. Conversely, it can accept a number that was already dismissed remotely. The command does not check the item's current open findings.
findings.title: Check dismissal numbers after reconciling the item's remote review

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - A close command requests two dismissals, the first open and the second already dismissed.
Every invocation in this test supplies only one --dismiss, although the Done-when requires checking each one. An implementation that validates only the first number would pass these cases while accepting the second invalid request and running tests or review. The command-level proof needs to cover that mixed request.
findings.title: Gate: test_1_unknown_dismissal_stops_before_tests_or_review

stop.reason: The owner wants one more round for all four findings, done simply: check the numbers after loading the latest review and change nothing else in the review records

why: A close with --dismiss runs the full tests and review, then refuses the dismissal because it checks only the new repair review's findings, so the whole run is wasted (#1253)
